key_highlights: ASX 200 closed the week higher despite intraday volatility, signalling resilience amid global uncertainty
Housing market under severe stress: auction sentiment deteriorating, 'perfect storm' warnings, and household terminations rising
Fixed mortgage rates edged higher into the weekend, adding pressure to rate-sensitive sectors
Pilbara mining activity booming; Gateway Resources adds 7km gold trend in WA, supporting materials sentiment
Consumer spending cautious: retailers report softening demand; EV uptake and weight-loss drug demand accelerating
Trump-Venezuela oil deal and data centre fossil-fuel policy create energy sector volatility
Qantas workforce redundancies signal ongoing pressure on transport and consumer discretionary

sectors.trend: Positive. Pilbara activity booming; Gateway Resources (GWR.AX) adds 7km gold trend in WA; ASX small-cap runners include Metal Hawk and Bapcor. Gold discovery supports sector sentiment.
sectors.implications: Supportive for BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX on iron ore demand; gold miners (GWR.AX, NGM.AX) benefit from discovery pipeline. Small-cap explorers attract speculative flows.

sectors.trend: Mixed. Trump-Venezuela oil deal introduces supply uncertainty; Australia's 'high bar' for fossil-fuel-powered data centres constrains gas demand growth; Hanson's coal-heavy policy lacks cost detail.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOC.AX face policy headwinds from data-centre restrictions; Santos (STO.AX) and Woodside (WDS.AX) benefit from any oil price volatility. Coal names (WES.AX) see political support but unclear economics.

sectors.trend: Cautious. Fixed mortgage rates edging higher; housing 'perfect storm' and auction deterioration threaten NIM and credit quality. Qantas redundancies signal broader economic softening.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from rate competition but benefit from higher yields. Credit risk rising in residential mortgage book. Monitor NIM compression.

sectors.trend: Negative. Retailers report cautious consumer spending; 'dupe' brand trend signals trade-down. EV uptake and weight-loss drug demand are bright spots.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WDW.AX, IAG.AX under pressure from weak discretionary spend. CSL.AX benefits from weight-loss drug demand. EV supply chain names see structural tailwind.

sectors.trend: Negative. Auction sentiment deteriorating sharply; 'perfect storm' warnings; household terminations rising. Housing inflation constrains RBA easing.
sectors.implications: Property REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICV.AX) face occupancy and valuation risk. Construction (WBC.AX exposure) and building materials under pressure. RBA constrained by sticky housing inflation.

sectors.trend: Positive. Nvidia AI chip futures market emerging globally; data centre build-out continues but faces Australian fossil-fuel power constraints. SpaceX-AI data centre disruption discussed.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (W1.AX, XRO.AX) benefit from global AI capex cycle. Data centre REITs and power infrastructure (SGH.AX, AGL.AX) see demand but face regulatory hurdles.

key_themes: Housing market stress as primary macro risk to RBA policy path
Consumer trade-down and cautious spending pattern
Commodity strength (gold, iron ore) supporting materials sector
Energy policy uncertainty: fossil-fuel data centres vs renewables transition
Global AI/tech capex cycle continuing but with new derivatives markets
Fixed-rate increases pressuring rate-sensitive borrowers and REITs

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce REIT and construction exposure; favour banks with strong capital buffers (CBA.AX, NAB.AX); monitor auction clearance rates weekly

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA policy constraint from sticky housing inflation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Position for prolonged higher-for-longer rate environment; favour dividend growers over rate-sensitive growth
Underweight discretionary retail (WDW.AX, IAG.AX); overweight staples (WES.AX, WOL.AX) and healthcare (CSL.AX)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Energy policy and geopolitical oil supply disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure; monitor Trump-Venezuela deal execution; diversify across WES.AX, WDS.AX, STO.AX

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Global debt / US fiscal risk spillover
risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain AUD hedge on offshore exposure; monitor US 10Y yields and Fed policy signals

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and iron ore miners on commodity strength and discovery pipeline
opportunities.rationale: Pilbara boom, Gateway 7km gold trend, and ASX small-cap momentum support materials sector outperformance

opportunities.recommendation: Add to healthcare and consumer staples on defensive rotation
opportunities.rationale: Consumer trade-down and weight-loss drug demand support CSL.AX; staples provide income in cautious environment

opportunities.recommendation: Selective energy exposure via gas majors on data centre demand
opportunities.rationale: Data centre build-out supports gas demand despite fossil-fuel policy headwinds; WDS.AX and STO.AX well-positioned

defensive_moves.rationale: Auction deterioration, 'perfect storm' warnings, and rising fixed rates create downside risk for property valuations

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim discretionary retail and transport exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Consumer caution, Qantas redundancies, and trade-down trend pressure WDW.AX, IAG.AX, QAN.AX

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain cash buffer and short-duration bonds
defensive_moves.rationale: Housing inflation constrains RBA easing; fixed rates still rising; preserve optionality for potential correction

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 likely to range-trade with volatility. Housing stress and consumer caution cap upside, but commodity strength and AI capex provide support. Fixed-rate increases add near-term pressure to rate-sensitive sectors. Expect 1-2% range over next 4-6 weeks.
market_outlook.long_term: Moderate growth outlook constrained by housing correction risk and RBA policy lag. Materials and healthcare offer relative outperformance. Energy sector bifurcated by policy. 6-12 month ASX 200 target: modest 3-5% gain if housing stabilises; downside 5-8% if correction accelerates.
